name: Corridor priority — which corridor link to protect first
summary: Computes the exact probability that two habitat cores stay connected and each link's pivotal probability, which the theorem shows is the reliability gradient, then ranks links for protection (optionally per unit cost).

reconciliation.note: The package's Lean status in the canon catalog is 'working' (not spine-admitted); Viridis OS admitted the DOI to its bundled canon index by the owner's decision on 2026-10-31, but the canon classification must be reconciled before admission as a function.

inputs.name: num_nodes
inputs.help: Number of habitat patches (nodes), numbered from 0.

inputs.name: edges
inputs.help: Corridor links as [node, node] pairs (at most 16).

inputs.name: survival
inputs.help: Survival probability of each link, in the same order; links are assumed to fail independently.

inputs.name: core_a
inputs.help: Nodes in the first habitat core.

inputs.name: core_b
inputs.help: Nodes in the second habitat core (disjoint from the first).

inputs.name: costs
inputs.help: Optional protection cost of each link, to rank by pivotal probability per unit cost.

hypotheses.statement: Every link survival probability is in [0, 1], one per link.
hypotheses.check: len(survival) == len(edges) and all(0 <= x <= 1 for x in survival)

hypotheses.statement: Both terminal cores name at least one node.

expected_outputs.scope: independent link survival; exact two-terminal reliability by enumeration

scope: Two-terminal reliability of an undirected corridor graph with independent link survival, by exact enumeration (at most 16 links).
boundary: Exact for independent link survival only. Correlated failures (fire, drought, a shared road), wrong survival probabilities, or a goal other than core-to-core connectivity are not covered, and the ranking is a first-order rule. The result is conditional on the supplied inputs; it does not establish empirical validity, Viridis review, certification, a credit, or a registry determination.
